scopeExpansions.justification: Objective 1 requires a *complete* caller map. These four files are the codebase's known cross-domain read-aggregation surfaces (per F2-PREP-002 INF-09/INF-10/INF-14/PAT-07); grepping them for any Imaging-model reference was necessary to affirmatively rule out an additional inbound caller, not merely to assume completeness from F2-PREP-002 alone. Result: zero matches in notifications.ts/dashboard.ts/reports.ts; platformAdmin.ts's only Imaging-relevant lines are the fileBackupService delegation already captured as IC-20.

F2-PREP-002's IMG domain slice groups Imaging together with Attachments/Inventory/Labs under one slice id. These four files share fileStorage.ts usage and analogous code comments with imaging.ts, creating surface-level ambiguity about whether they are Imaging callers. Direct grep for every Imaging Prisma model name confirmed zero matches in all four — they are same-shape siblings (Attachments/Labs domains), not Imaging callers, and are correctly excluded from this task's scope.

transactionFlows.description: Pre-write phase common to both upload paths: authentication (staff role or bridge-token), rate-limit/concurrency-cap check, request-body/multipart validation, file-signature (magic-byte) validation, and — bridge path only — server-side sha256 recomputation of the client-claimed ingestKey (client value never trusted).
The physical storage write itself: saveFile(storageKey, buffer, mime). A single call, atomic in isolation, but NOT part of the subsequent DB transaction.
transactionFlows.atomicWithRespectTo: storage only, not jointly with the DB write

transactionFlows.description: DB-only `$transaction`: ImagingStudy create + ImagingImage create + guarded ImagingRequest.updateMany (status flip to 'received', re-checked against IN (requested,scheduled) to avoid clobbering a race). Bridge path additionally handles a P2002 (clinicId,ingestKey) unique-constraint race by deleting the just-written file and returning the pre-existing study as duplicate.

All other field mutations on ImagingDevice/ImagingRequest/ImagingStudy/ImagingBridgeAgent/ImagingBridgePairing outside the upload path (see statusMutationBypasses and the full field table in the narrative doc). Sequential read-then-write with no lock in every case except the two hard-delete paths.

NOT IMPLEMENTED in this codebase snapshot. No DICOM-to-preview conversion, thumbnail generation, or CBCT slice-extraction pipeline was found anywhere in the inspected paths. streamStudyImage() serves original bytes directly (with a documented DICOM-vs-other-format branch for preview handling, not a conversion job). This is consistent with docs/program/phases/F10_IMAGING_DICOM_AND_AI.md describing DICOM/AI processing as a FUTURE phase, not yet built — noted for completeness, not independently verified against that phase document (out of this task's scope).
transactionFlows.evidence: grep across services/imaging/*, jobs/*: zero conversion/processing job found

transactionFlows.description: Set either at upload time (via imagingRequestId inheritance or direct params) or later via PATCH .../link (replaces existing links) / PATCH .../unlink (nulls all links + imagingRequestId, but does NOT reopen an already-'received' ImagingRequest — treated as an audit trail, a documented Phase-1 limitation).
transactionFlows.evidence: imaging.ts L559-611 (inheritance), L807-854 (link), L859-892 (unlink, comment L857-858)

transactionFlows.description: NOT IMPLEMENTED / absent by design. See SUB-01.

ImagingDevice and ImagingBridgeAgent support a real, gated, atomic hard delete (`$transaction` + `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, blocked if in-use). ImagingStudy supports archive/unarchive (idempotent status flip, non-atomic but low-risk single-field write) but is NEVER deleted. ImagingImage is never deleted or updated at the route layer (only via the two metadata-mutation service functions above). ImagingRequest and ImagingBridgePairing are never deleted, only status-terminalized.
transactionFlows.atomic: mixed — device/agent delete is atomic; archive/unarchive is not (and does not need to be, single field)
transactionFlows.evidence: imaging.ts L339-400, L894-921, L1080-1140; imaging.test.ts L256-261; kvkkAttachmentImagingLifecycle.test.ts L1250-1253

transactionFlows.description: Only the bridge study-ingest path has a real retry/idempotency mechanism: a retried upload of the same file bytes (same or different bridge agent, since dedupe is clinic-scoped, not agent-scoped) short-circuits to `{ ok:true, studyId, duplicate:true }` via a pre-check findFirst and, for the true concurrent-race case, a P2002 catch. No other Imaging entity (device, request, pairing, manual upload) has any retry/idempotency key — each is a one-shot, non-idempotent create.
transactionFlows.evidence: imagingBridgePublic.ts L257-267, L343-359; schema.prisma @@unique([clinicId, ingestKey]) on ImagingStudy

transactionFlows.description: Forward direction (DB row exists, storage object missing) IS covered: orphanFileInspection.ts's inspectOrphans()/markConfirmedMissing(), manually triggered per-patient, not a background sweep. Reverse direction (storage object exists, no DB row — the exact failure mode created by FP-01/FP-02) is NOT covered by any job or service in the inspected paths; the only mitigation is the best-effort, non-retried `catch`-block deleteFile() at upload time, which itself does nothing if the process dies before reaching it.
transactionFlows.evidence: orphanFileInspection.ts L16-22 (header explicitly states reverse-orphan detection is not implemented and would require an unbounded storage scan the architecture avoids); imaging.ts L684; imagingBridgePublic.ts L385

atomicOperations.mechanism: $transaction (no row lock; guarded updateMany for the ImagingRequest status flip)
single updateMany statement (DB-atomic on its own, no explicit $transaction needed)

eventualOperations.shape: read-then-write, no lock, no guarded updateMany
sequential, no lock, narrow race vs. concurrent heartbeat
cancel side unlocked; redemption side locked — asymmetric
two independent systems (object storage + Postgres) with no joint atomicity; compensated only by a best-effort catch-block cleanup

eventualOperations.operation: fileBackupService cross-tenant enumeration + per-file ledger writes
eventualOperations.shape: not atomic per-file, but self-healing across runs (idempotent-safe — a crash mid-file just means the next run re-attempts it)

eventualOperations.operation: patientAnonymization / orphanFileInspection per-row loops over ImagingImage
eventualOperations.shape: explicitly non-atomic, partial-failure-tolerant by design (each row independently try/catch'd, failures counted and surfaced, never rolled back)

failurePoints.description: Crash/process-death between storage saveFile() success and DB $transaction commit, manual upload path -> orphaned storage object with no ImagingImage row, undetectable by any existing job (no reverse-orphan scan exists).
Identical failure mode, bridge upload path.
The compensating catch-block deleteFile() call itself swallows its own failure (`.catch(() => {})`) with no retry and no logging-as-inconsistency — if cleanup fails, the orphan is silently permanent.

markConfirmedMissing() trusts caller-supplied entries without re-validating clinic/patient scope inside the function itself — a latent IDOR if this function is ever wired to a route accepting less-trusted input. No such route currently exists in the inspected paths.

patientAnonymization's per-row ImagingImage redaction loop can partially succeed (some rows redacted, others not) within a single anonymization call, with the failure count surfaced but no rollback — by explicit design, but still a real partial-state outcome for a KVKK-irreversible operation.

ImagingRequest PATCH: two concurrent PATCHes can both read the same stale existing.status outside a lock and clobber each other — unlike the upload path's guarded updateMany, there is no equivalent guard here.

ImagingBridgePairing cancel (staff-side, DELETE) has no lock while /pair redemption (bridge-side) does — a pairing being redeemed concurrently with a staff cancel is not fully race-proof on the cancel side.

ImagingBridgeAgent revoke vs. a concurrent heartbeat: authenticateBridgeAgent is re-checked before the heartbeat's own update, but a revoke landing between that check and the update is a narrow, unlocked window.

The pairing attempt-count increment on an unexpected failure path is itself inside the same $transaction as the main redemption logic — if that increment's own update fails, the whole transaction rolls back and the failed attempt is never counted, silently losing part of the audit trail for that edge case.

compensationRequirements.requirement: A reverse-orphan reconciliation job (storage object exists, no DB row) — currently absent. Needed before Imaging's storage responsibility can be treated as safely extractable to a separate service/process boundary without accepting a known, currently-silent consistency gap.
A durable/retried (not fire-and-forget) compensation for deleteFile() failure in the upload catch path, or an accepted, explicitly-documented eventual-consistency contract in its place.
A lock or guarded updateMany for ImagingRequest PATCH, mirroring the upload path's own guarded status-flip pattern, before ImagingRequest mutation is exposed as an external contract.
A lock or optimistic version check on ImagingStudy link/unlink to remove last-write-wins ambiguity under concurrent staff edits.
A re-scope (clinic/patient) check inside markConfirmedMissing() itself, as defense-in-depth, before this function is ever exposed to any less-trusted caller via a future ImagingLifecyclePort.

An explicit, accepted eventual-consistency contract (or transactional wrapping, if a future decision requires it) documented for patientAnonymization's per-row ImagingImage redaction, before Imaging's data can be owned by a service independent of Privacy's anonymization sweep.

idempotencyRequirements.mechanism: unique(clinicId, ingestKey) DB constraint + P2002 catch + pre-check findFirst
idempotencyRequirements.requirement: PRESERVE this exact mechanism across any future extraction — the uniqueness guarantee must move with the model or be replaced by an equivalent guarantee in any new service's own store.

idempotencyRequirements.mechanism: no ingestKey; every call creates a new row unconditionally
idempotencyRequirements.requirement: Flag as a gap only if retry semantics are ever required at the UI/client level for this path — no such requirement observed in the current code.
Acceptable for their current interactive, staff-initiated usage pattern; would need a client-supplied idempotency key added only if any future async/queued caller is introduced.

idempotencyRequirements.mechanism: repeated runs of the same updateMany converge to the same state
row-locked status check prevents double-redemption of the same code

migrationOrder.action: Replace SMB-01/SMB-02 (Privacy's direct metadata-mutation writes to ImagingImage) with the already-named F2-PREP-002 F2-CC-14 contract (ImagingLifecyclePort.markStorageMissing()/redactForAnonymization()).
migrationOrder.rationale: Smallest surface, clearest and already-agreed target shape, lowest number of call sites (2).

migrationOrder.action: Replace DAV-01/DAV-02 (Privacy's direct reads for deletion-review and orphan-inspection) with a query-side extension of the same port.
migrationOrder.rationale: Same port family as step 1; consolidates Privacy's entire Imaging touchpoint behind one contract.

migrationOrder.action: Harden ImagingRequest PATCH concurrency internally (CR-03) before any external caller of request-mutation is ever added.
migrationOrder.rationale: Pre-extraction hardening, not a caller migration — but a blocking prerequisite for safely exposing ImagingRequest mutation as a contract later.

migrationOrder.action: Formalize the existing bridge-agent public surface (imagingBridgePublic.ts) as the documented external module boundary.
migrationOrder.rationale: Already structurally isolated (own router, own token-based auth, own rate limiting) — F2-PREP-002 IMG-01 already calls it a 'well-hardened de-facto public contract'; requires documentation, not code change.

migrationOrder.action: Address the storage/DB two-phase gap (CR-01/CR-02) before Imaging's storage responsibility is extracted behind a real network boundary.
migrationOrder.rationale: Highest-risk unresolved item — a real network hop between a future Imaging service and its database would widen the existing in-process crash window, not merely preserve it.

migrationOrder.action: Leave DAV-03/DAV-07 (fileBackupService's read-only cross-tenant enumeration of ImagingImage) for last.
migrationOrder.rationale: Lowest risk (read-only, never mutates Imaging data); F2-PREP-002 already proposed treating the equivalent INF-07 edge as an accepted PUBLIC_CONTRACT_CANDIDATE rather than an urgent violation.

temporaryCompatibilityNeeds.need: A thin pass-through compatibility facade with an identical return shape to today's direct Prisma reads, if DAV-01/DAV-02 (Privacy's reads) are migrated to the new port on a different release cadence than Privacy's own consuming code.

None identified for SMB-01/SMB-02 — F2-CC-14 already fully specifies the target command shape, and both call sites are internal service functions (not routes), so no external client compatibility window is needed.

blockers.description: No reverse-orphan reconciliation job exists (CR-01) and the existing forward compensation is best-effort/non-retried (CR-02) — treating Imaging's storage responsibility as independently extractable today means knowingly accepting this consistency gap, not closing it.
blockers.mustResolveBefore: Extracting Imaging's storage/upload path behind a real service or network boundary

blockers.description: ImagingRequest PATCH has no concurrency guard (FP-06/CR-03) equivalent to the upload path's guarded updateMany.
blockers.mustResolveBefore: Exposing ImagingRequest mutation as an external contract to any caller outside imaging.ts itself
